parameterHelp.label: Parameter guide
parameterHelp.diagramExample: Illustration values do not change task parameters.
parameterHelp.chunkDescription: Long audio is processed in separate chunks.
parameterHelp.chunkTakeaway: Longer chunks provide more context and usually use more VRAM.
parameterHelp.chunkDetail: chunk_size is measured in samples. Chunk duration is the sample count divided by the inference sample rate; larger chunks do not guarantee better separation.
parameterHelp.overlapDescription: Adjacent chunks share audio and join their results in the overlap region.
parameterHelp.overlapTakeaway: More overlap can reduce boundary artifacts but requires more computation.
parameterHelp.overlapDetail: overlap_size is measured in samples and takes precedence over num_overlap. The ratio depends on both overlap length and chunk size.
parameterHelp.vrWindowDescription: VR models process audio in spectral windows.
parameterHelp.vrWindowTakeaway: Larger windows usually use more VRAM.
parameterHelp.vrWindowDetail: window_size is measured in spectral frames, unlike the samples used by chunk_size. Supported values depend on the model.
parameterHelp.vrAggressionDescription: Controls the strength of VR spectral mask processing.
parameterHelp.vrAggressionTakeaway: Higher values may reduce bleed but can also suppress the target source.
parameterHelp.vrAggressionDetail: aggression ranges from 0 to 100. Higher values strengthen mask processing but may introduce distortion or artifacts.
parameterHelp.videoReference: 20% is a video reference, not a model default.
parameterHelp.overlapCalculation: Overlap: {overlap} samples ({seconds} s). Each step advances {hop} s.
parameterHelp.msstFormula: MSST conversion: overlap_size = chunk_size − ⌊chunk_size ÷ {count}⌋. Integer rounding may slightly change the ratio.
parameterHelp.exampleOnly: Calculated at 44,100 Hz. Empty or zero chunk and overlap values use the default configuration; zero overlap does not disable overlap.
parameterHelp.batchDetail: Larger batches can improve hardware utilization but require more VRAM. Reducing the batch can help with out-of-memory errors. Task concurrency is a separate setting.
parameterHelp.ttaDetail: Channel swapping exchanges left and right, not playback direction. Polarity inversion negates the waveform. Both transformations are undone before averaging. For mono audio, swapping channels leaves the input unchanged.
parameterHelp.standardizeDetail: Standardization gives zero mean and unit variance; it does not turn arbitrary audio into a normal distribution. Output is multiplied by the original standard deviation and shifted by the mean. Constant or silent input is not scaled.
parameterHelp.normalizeDetail: Peak normalization applies a constant gain to the whole audio signal so its target peak is below 0 dBFS. It does not compress dynamics or match perceived loudness. Summing multiple stems may still exceed full scale.
parameterHelp.ttaDescription: Runs the original, channel-swapped, and polarity-inverted audio through the model, then restores and averages the results.
parameterHelp.ttaTakeaway: Three inference passes take longer and do not guarantee better separation.
parameterHelp.vrTtaDescription: Predicts masks at two spectral window positions, then aligns and averages them.
parameterHelp.vrTtaTakeaway: VR shifts windows rather than swapping channels or inverting polarity.
parameterHelp.vrTtaDetail: The second pass shifts the window by half its effective length. Its mask is aligned with the first prediction before averaging, adding computation.
parameterHelp.standardizeDescription: Subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation before inference, then restores the original amplitude scale.
parameterHelp.standardizeTakeaway: Acts on model input and should match the model's preprocessing requirements.
parameterHelp.normalizeDescription: When output peaks exceed 0 dBFS, reduces the whole signal by a constant gain to bring peaks below full scale.
parameterHelp.normalizeTakeaway: The diagram shows peak attenuation; quieter audio may also be amplified.
parameterHelp.batchDescription: Audio chunks sent through the model together, rather than the number of files processed concurrently.
parameterHelp.batchTakeaway: Affects speed and VRAM usage, not a separation quality level.
parameterHelp.bitDepthDescription: If output peaks still exceed 0 dBFS, saving as 16/24-bit integer PCM clips those samples. WAV FLOAT can retain them.
parameterHelp.bitDepthTakeaway: Choose WAV FLOAT to retain peaks above full scale. Normalize or lower the level before saving as integer PCM.
parameterHelp.bitDepthDetail: Normalization or lower gain can bring peaks within full scale and avoid clipping when saving integer PCM. The main differences between 16-bit and 24-bit are quantization precision and file size; more bits do not add headroom above full scale. FLOAT uses 32-bit floating point without changing model predictions.
parameterHelp.bitDepthPcm16: 16-bit integer. Samples above 0 dBFS clip when saved.
parameterHelp.bitDepthPcm24: 24-bit integer. Samples above 0 dBFS still clip when saved.
parameterHelp.bitDepthFloat: 32-bit floating-point WAV. Retains samples above 0 dBFS without clipping them at full scale.
parameterHelp.bitDepthNote: FLOAT cannot repair earlier clipping. Lower retained peaks above full scale before playback or conversion to integer PCM.
parameterHelp.bitRateDescription: Bitrate is the data used for encoding each second, measured in kbps. MP3 and AAC have different selectable limits.
parameterHelp.aacBitRateLimit: AAC: up to 512 kbps in this app. AAC encoders may support higher rates.
parameterHelp.bitRateTakeaway: Higher rates usually mean larger files and less compression loss, without restoring lost detail.
parameterHelp.bitRateDetail: The illustration starts at 320 kbps and assumes 60 seconds at a fixed bitrate: audio data size is approximately bitrate times duration divided by 8. MP3 offers up to 320 kbps; this app offers AAC up to 512 kbps. Actual AAC support depends on the encoder and audio parameters. Containers and variable bitrate affect file size.

diagram.attenuatePeak: Reduce gain when peaks exceed full scale
diagram.batchCost: Larger batches usually need more VRAM

beginnerGuide.label: Getting started
beginnerGuide.inviteDescription: An introduction to models, separation, audio editing, and workflows.
beginnerGuide.paused: The guide is paused. You can keep exploring other pages.
beginnerGuide.runtimePaused: Prepare a runtime first, then continue the guide after installation.
beginnerGuide.modePaused: Switch to single-model separation to continue the guide.
beginnerGuide.modelDescription: Models specialize in different sources. Cards show targets, architecture, and size; stars mark favorites.
beginnerGuide.inputDescription: Accepts audio, video, folders, and dropped files. Multiple files are processed as a batch.
beginnerGuide.outputDescription: The save location for this task. An empty field uses the default folder from Settings.
beginnerGuide.runDescription: Submits separation with the current model and parameters. Each input file is processed separately.
beginnerGuide.chunkFieldDescription: Samples per inference chunk determine the available audio context. Larger values use more VRAM without guaranteeing better separation.
beginnerGuide.overlapFieldDescription: Samples shared by adjacent chunks. More overlap can reduce boundary artifacts, at the cost of additional computation and time.
beginnerGuide.overlapCountFieldDescription: MSST-compatible overlap count: 2 is about 50%, and 4 about 75%. An explicit overlap length takes precedence.
beginnerGuide.windowFieldDescription: Spectral frames per VR inference window. Larger windows usually use more VRAM; supported values depend on the model.
beginnerGuide.aggressionFieldDescription: VR mask strength, from 0 to 100. Higher values may reduce bleed but can also suppress the target source.
beginnerGuide.inferenceDescription: Controls chunking, overlap, batch size, and preprocessing during inference.
beginnerGuide.encodingDescription: Controls encoding precision, compression, and output volume processing.
beginnerGuide.ttaFieldDescription: Combines predictions from multiple input transformations. It takes longer; any improvement depends on the model.
beginnerGuide.postProcessFieldDescription: Corrects artifacts in the VR separation mask, using the post-processing threshold to identify affected regions.
beginnerGuide.postThresholdFieldDescription: VR post-processing threshold, from 0 to 1. Applies only when post-processing is enabled.
beginnerGuide.highEndFieldDescription: Reconstructs high-frequency content in VR output through spectral mirroring. Results depend on the model and input.
beginnerGuide.wavFieldDescription: If output peaks still exceed 0 dBFS, saving as 16/24-bit integer PCM clips those samples. FLOAT can retain them.
beginnerGuide.flacFieldDescription: Both 16-bit and 24-bit FLAC use integer PCM, which clips samples above 0 dBFS. Switch to WAV FLOAT to retain those peaks.
beginnerGuide.mp3FieldDescription: Target MP3 bitrate, up to 320 kbps. Higher values usually reduce compression loss and increase file size.
beginnerGuide.m4aFieldDescription: Target AAC bitrate. This app offers up to 512 kbps. AAC can support higher rates depending on the encoder and audio parameters.
beginnerGuide.codecFieldDescription: The audio encoder used for M4A files, currently AAC.
beginnerGuide.modelDefaultsDescription: Saves inference parameters for future tasks using this model. Restore removes the model's custom defaults.
beginnerGuide.durationNote: Uses temporary data. Your files and settings stay unchanged.
beginnerGuide.queueDescription: Shows task progress, status, and logs, with cancellation and failure details.
beginnerGuide.resultsDescription: Lists completed tasks, output stems, and file locations, with search, filters, and sorting.
beginnerGuide.filtersDescription: Filter by keyword, category, or source. Downloaded only lists locally available models.
beginnerGuide.managementDescription: Imports models and matching configurations. Storage management shows disk usage and deletes models or residual files.
beginnerGuide.managementMacDescription: Storage management shows local disk usage and supports model deletion and residual cleanup.
beginnerGuide.ensembleDescription: Blends matching stems from several models using algorithms and weights. Model choice affects results and processing time.
beginnerGuide.workflowDescription: Stores reusable processing configurations, with simple editing, advanced node editing, and configuration imports.
beginnerGuide.workflowRunDescription: Previews node connections, output stems, and model readiness. The editor controls nodes and their parameters.
beginnerGuide.runtimeDescription: Installs, switches, and updates CPU, CUDA, and ROCm runtimes, and shows dependency and driver status.
beginnerGuide.runtimeMacDescription: Shows MLX runtime health, dependencies, and separation core versions, with core updates.
beginnerGuide.helpDescription: Getting started introduces the main features. The parameter guide illustrates inference, volume processing, and encoding settings.
beginnerGuide.workspaceDescription: Separation processes audio, Models manages models, and Results lists tasks and outputs.
beginnerGuide.selectionDescription: The downloaded model used for this task. It determines available stems and default inference parameters.
beginnerGuide.formatDescription: WAV and FLAC are lossless; MP3 and M4A are lossy. Layered layout groups files by input; flat layout uses one folder.
beginnerGuide.stemsDescription: Available stems depend on the model, such as vocals or instruments. Unchecked stems are not saved.
beginnerGuide.namingDescription: Filenames support placeholders for the input name, stem, and sequence number. The output path is previewed.
beginnerGuide.editorDescription: Supports playback, trimming, volume and pan adjustments, and mix export.
beginnerGuide.workflowModeDescription: Model mode uses a separation model; workflow mode runs a saved processing configuration. Both share input and output settings.
beginnerGuide.pathsDescription: The model folder stores models; the default output folder stores results. Separation can use a task-specific output location.
beginnerGuide.deviceDescription: The default device for new tasks, including CPU and GPUs available in the current runtime.
beginnerGuide.deviceMacDescription: MLX uses the Apple Silicon GPU to accelerate inference.
beginnerGuide.downloadsDescription: Configures model sources, download methods, and network proxies, with a proxy connection test.
beginnerGuide.toolsOverviewDescription: Provides format conversion, audio inspection, slicing, merging, and loudness processing.
beginnerGuide.editorPlaybackDescription: Playback, pause, and timeline seeking control listening. Master volume sets the overall level.
beginnerGuide.editorMixDescription: M mutes a track; S isolates soloed tracks. The track inspector controls volume, pan, and effects.
beginnerGuide.editorExportDescription: Renders the timeline as WAV or FLAC, with bit depth, sample rate, and peak protection settings.
beginnerGuide.workflowEditorDescription: Nodes represent models or processing operations. Connections route audio; parameters control each node.
beginnerGuide.workflowOutputDescription: Output format, save locations, and device settings are saved with the workflow for reuse.
beginnerGuide.editorClipsDescription: Clips support movement, trimming, and fades. Timeline edits leave source files unchanged.
